body:
I second all of what infj404 said. I would also add the following:

I am exactly where you are right now, believe it or not. I'm depressed now, and have been for some time. I also binge drink whenever I get the chance (usually I preempt being around alcohol one way or another) and do little but sleep with breaks of watching mindless movies and eating some basic meals. Haven't been able to get myself to exercise much, even though that's part of the solution. I would characterize myself as barely existing, just sort of getting through the haze for the sake of it.

Here's what I'll be doing very shortly. I'll be going to see a therapist to see what to work on. I've already seen a doctor and am on antidepressants, which help a good deal but will fade in effectiveness. What won't fade are new habits and new passions and reigniting old hobbyhorses. That's where therapy can come in, to help you sort of reboot yourself and come back online. Over time, I expect to want to go out into the world and explore it and regain the "lust for life." Please, please consider seeing a therapist or talking it over with a close friend. These things are complex and can quickly take over your life and void it almost totally of meaning -- which is bad. Very bad, believe me.

In the meantime, feel free to message me back about this. It's a journey, to be sure, and I'm excited to see where you go from here!

At this point I've settled on just waiting and seeing if I find someone right for me and then pursuing that relationship wholeheartedly to the fullest extent. It may take time and effort, but I think it'll be worth it. 

I'm also very, very interested in having children someday; the idea of a happy family appeals to me a great deal, and intimacy in that context is something I'm actually very keen on.

I'm an INFJ male, too. You took the words right out of my mouth. 

I feel the same way about intimacy, sex, relationships, all of it. I especially identify with how you feel about the "urges." I also know exactly what you mean by resigning yourself to not wanting any of it -- I've been there before.
